html:
SMTO-HTTP-0061 — The Agent didn't use the saved connection for this address

GUID: 49cdcbd5-4e10-4abd-a556-71173d86d3cc
Slug: http-verified-profile-required
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • SMTO found one saved connection that fits this web address, but the Agent's request didn't choose it. SMTO stopped the request so it isn't sent without the right sign-in. Nothing was sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait for the Agent to continue. SMTO tells it which saved connection matches and lets it correct itself up to two times. The Agent can usually pick the matching saved connection on its own.
  2. If the Run stops, look up the connection's name in Parameter Store and reply in the Conversation asking the Agent to use that saved connection. Naming the saved connection makes the Agent send the request with the right sign-in.
  3. If you meant to use a different account for this address, tell the Agent clearly which other saved connection to use. A different connection is allowed when you choose it on purpose.

What success looks like

  • The Agent's next web request goes through using the saved connection and its result appears in the Conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Nothing was sent to the other service, so you don't need to check it for changes.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Exactly one verified saved-profile setup matches the request URL, but http.request supplied neither its current connection_ref, the profile_key, nor an explicit alternate configuration, so the routing.http_reuse guard rejected it without dispatch.

What this means

  • Exactly one verified saved-profile setup matches the URL, but the request supplies neither its current connection reference nor the required profile selector or explicit alternate configuration. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Exactly one verified saved-profile setup matches the URL, but the request supplies neither its current connection reference nor the required profile selector or explicit alternate configuration.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the matched verified setup and its exact profile key; do not infer authentication from the URL alone.

How to fix it

  • Use the verified profile_key (or the current connection_ref) advertised by the guard for that origin, or provide an explicit alternate profile, auth or base URL that passes ordinary validation. The model gets two correction attempts before the run is blocked with http_reuse_correction_limit.
  • Use the verified profile and current connection reference returned by supported discovery, or explicitly configure a different intended connection through its secure flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended verified profile/current reference is selected and passes ordinary admission.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
